summary: The test itself is good and does what criterion 1 and criterion 2 ask. Verified against the production code rather than against the prose: the three cases really do elicit three different modes (inline via heldSegmentKey == SEGMENT_KEY and a 1 MiB cap; proxy via coldMode with directEnabled=false, which lands on streamFromStore because held is null; direct via coldMode with directEnabled=true, presign=true, fanOut 1 <= 4), and containsOnly(expected) pins each one off the push the consumer was handed rather than off the policy. The direct case's bytes genuinely come from the fetch: the DIRECT arm passes `sinks -> { }`, AssemblingSubscriber's sink therefore yields a zero-length `whole`, and ConsumerClient.bytesOf must call SegmentSource or SegmentReader.open throws on an empty array -- so the mutation `bytesOf -> return delivery.segment()` reds this test. Criterion 2 is genuinely observed from outside: HubBridge registers a fresh assembling Subscriber per subscribe, so two ConsumerClients give targets.size() == 2 against a threshold of 1, and dropping the fan-out conjunct in FetchPolicy.wantsDirect reds both the modesSeen assertion and the neverCalled source. Everything is synchronous through deliver(), so the 200 ms polls are not a race. No production code is touched and no object-store request rate moves: the ingester issues one GET on the proxy path only (streamFromStore, per segment, which is where it already was) and zero on direct; the consumer issues one fetch per delivery, which is the per-run rate M5.45h owns by name and which this row's own backlog cell correctly declines to claim. What I am blocking on is not the test but its placement and the evidence recorded for it. The premise the new build edge rests on -- 'No module sees both ingest (which serves) and client (which decodes)' -- is false, and the gate cited as clearing the edge cannot see test configurations at all.

findings.title: the premise for the new `http` -> `client` edge is false: `plugin/src/test` already sees both `ingest` and `client`, and already contains the bridge
findings.failure_scenario: The comment states 'No module sees both `ingest` (which serves) and `client` (which decodes)' and the test javadoc (ThreeModesAgreeTest.java:59-66) repeats it. plugin/build.gradle.kts already declares `api(project(":client"))` and `testImplementation(project(":ingest"))` plus `testImplementation(project(":binstore-backends"))`, so plugin's test source set sees both halves and binstore-spi as well -- and plugin/src/test/java/binjava/plugin/EndToEndTest.java:66 already carries the hub-to-consumer bridge this test re-implements as HubBridge, with the same `hub.subscribe(key, SubscriptionHub.assembling(push -> listener.onDelivery(new Delivery(...))))` body, and already imports binjava.binstore.CountingBinStore and binjava.binstore.backend.LocalFsBinStore, so ADR-0023 is no obstacle there either (it governs src/main). ThreeModesAgreeTest compiles and runs unchanged under plugin/src/test with ZERO build changes. Concrete failure, two of them. (1) The tree gains a dependency edge nobody needed: every other edge in the tree, production or test, points backwards along settings.gradle.kts's declared dependency order (binstore-spi, binstore-backends, format, sequencer, ingest, http, client, plugin); `http` -> `client` is the first forward edge, from the producer-side `_bulk` adapter to the consumer library, and it is the one an author of a future test will cite as precedent -- the comment literally offers itself as one ('the same argument the two dependencies above already rest on', which is not the same argument: binstore-backends and sequencer are both BELOW http, client is not). (2) A false statement about the module graph is committed in a build file and in a test javadoc, where the next reader deciding where to put a hub-plus-client test will believe it and add a second such edge rather than looking at plugin. The fix is to move the file to plugin/src/test/java/binjava/plugin/ and drop the build change entirely; if it stays in `http`, the comment must stop claiming no module sees both and must instead say why plugin was rejected.

findings.title: criterion 3's recorded evidence is a gate that structurally cannot observe a `testImplementation` edge, and it is not the check the criterion names
findings.failure_scenario: The cell records '⚠️ CRITERION 3 ASSERTED: `GATE_SCOPE=full ./scripts/check-module.sh` green with the new test-only edge, 8 modules checked'. scripts/check-module.sh resolves exactly two configurations per module -- `for conf in runtimeClasspath compileClasspath` (line ~336) -- which are the MAIN source set's. A `testImplementation` dependency never appears in either, so every rule that file applies (rule 4's `project ':http'` grep, rule 5's HTTP_GROUPS grep, rule 2's binstore-backends and cloud-SDK greps) was evaluated over bytes in which the new edge does not appear. The gate would have printed the identical '8 module(s) checked' line with the edge absent, with the edge reversed to `testImplementation(project(":http"))` in client, or with anything else added under a test configuration. It is green, it was run, and it asserted nothing whatsoever about the thing it is cited for -- the packet's own lens for this change ('confirm it cannot pass vacuously'). Concrete failure: the cell is permanent and is the record a future row reads; the next person adding a cross-branch test-only edge cites 'check-module is green with it' as clearance, and the first edge that actually matters -- a test-only `project(":http")` somewhere below http, which drags Helidon onto a test classpath rule 5 exists to keep clear -- gets the same green with nobody having looked. Separately, criterion 3's words are 'ADR-0023's dependency check green, asserted', and that check is not check-module: ADR-0023 states it as the hand-run grep over plugin/src/main and client/src/main (M1.16e, still todo), which M5.45g's own cell ran and reported, and which this cell does not mention. The substance holds -- this change touches neither src/main -- but the evidence named is the wrong check on top of being a vacuous one. Record what was actually run, and say plainly that check-module does not see test configurations.

findings.title: the criterion's words are 'byte for byte' and the comparison is a lossy UTF-8 string projection
findings.failure_scenario: bodies() reduces each ConsumerRecord to `offset + ":" + id + ":" + new String(payload, UTF_8)`, dropping SegmentRecord.opType(), SegmentRecord.version() and ConsumerRecord.timestampMillis(), and comparing the payload through a UTF-8 decode rather than as bytes. Concrete failure: a future change that made one mode's path lose the version or the op type -- for instance a delivery-level re-encode added on the direct path, which is the one mode where the bytes do not travel with the push -- would deliver INDEX/OptionalLong.empty() where the others deliver INDEX/OptionalLong.of(1), and all three assertions here stay green while the milestone's headline criterion is exactly what broke. Any payload byte sequence that is not valid UTF-8 also compares equal to any other that decodes to the same U+FFFD run; the fixture is pure ASCII JSON so nothing is masked today, but the assertion no longer says what the criterion says. Comparing (offset, id, opType, version, timestampMillis) with the payload asserted via assertThat(byte[]).isEqualTo(byte[]) costs nothing here and restores the literal claim. Recorded as minor because no mutation of the code as it stands survives it.
